# linux_stat (Data Source)

Tells whether a path exists and what it is, like Ansible's `stat`: use it to test that a file or a directory exists. A missing path is not an error: `exists` is `false` and the other attributes are null.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "linux_stat" "docker_socket" {
  path = "/var/run/docker.sock"
}

data "linux_stat" "data_dir" {
  path   = "/srv/data"
  follow = true
}

output "docker_installed" {
  value = data.linux_stat.docker_socket.exists
}

output "data_dir_is_directory" {
  value = data.linux_stat.data_dir.type == "directory"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path.

### Optional

- `follow` (Boolean) Describe the target of a symbolic link rather than the link. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `exists` (Boolean) Whether something exists at the path.
- `gid` (Number) Group ID.
- `group` (String) Group name, or GID when it has none.
- `id` (String) The path.
- `link_target` (String) Target of a symbolic link.
- `mode` (String) Permissions, as four octal digits.
- `owner` (String) Owner name, or UID when it has none.
- `size` (Number) Size in bytes.
- `type` (String) `file`, `directory`, `symlink` or `other`.
- `uid` (Number) Owner ID.
